svg.title: Quantum phase estimation
svg.text: Phase estimation reads a phase off turning qubit dials
Controlled U turns counting qubit j by 2^j times the phase φ; the inverse QFT turns those angles into a reading of φ, the eigenphase of U.
Start: 4 counting qubits, each 0 and 1 at once; the target qubit holds |1⟩
Controlled U×1 on q0: its dial turns by 1 × φ
Controlled U×2 on q1: its dial turns by 2 × φ
Controlled U×4 on q2: its dial turns by 4 × φ
Controlled U×8 on q3: its dial turns by 8 × φ
Inverse QFT: the 4 angles become one likely 4-bit reading
5 counting qubits: readings 1/32 of a turn apart, bunched around φ
6 counting qubits: readings 1/64 of a turn apart, bunched around φ
7 counting qubits: readings 1/128 of a turn apart, bunched around φ
8 counting qubits: readings 1/256 of a turn apart, bunched around φ
Counting qubits after their controlled-U steps (before the inverse QFT)
hand = the phase each qubit picked up, clockwise from 12, in turns · U×k = U applied k times under that qubit's control
U = Rz(θ) leaves |1⟩ as it is apart from a phase, φ of a turn: the number we want.
The target does not change; the phase kicks back onto q0: 1 × 0.0833 → 0.083 turn (whole turns drop out).
The target does not change; the phase kicks back onto q1: 2 × 0.0833 → 0.167 turn (whole turns drop out).
The target does not change; the phase kicks back onto q2: 4 × 0.0833 → 0.333 turn (whole turns drop out).
The target does not change; the phase kicks back onto q3: 8 × 0.0833 → 0.667 turn (whole turns drop out).
The angles φ, 2φ, 4φ, 8φ hold φ's binary digits; the inverse QFT turns them into a number.
Each extra qubit turns twice as far again: one more binary digit of φ (q4: U×16).
Each extra qubit turns twice as far again: one more binary digit of φ (q5: U×32).
Each extra qubit turns twice as far again: one more binary digit of φ (q6: U×64).
Each extra qubit turns twice as far again: one more binary digit of φ (q7: U×128).
Chance of each reading of the counting qubits
reading k of n bits means φ ≈ k/2^n of a turn · E = −2π × φ for the stand-in H = (θ/2)·Z, as the script prints it
Read now, all 16 readings are equally likely: the angles do not show in the counts.
Off by 0.0208 of a turn; neighbouring readings are 0.0625 apart
Off by 0.0104 of a turn; neighbouring readings are 0.0312 apart
Off by 0.0052 of a turn; neighbouring readings are 0.0156 apart
Off by 0.0026 of a turn; neighbouring readings are 0.0078 apart
Off by 0.0013 of a turn; neighbouring readings are 0.0039 apart
